requiredExposures.note: Add load after exceeding the target on two consecutive sessions. The only source; ACSM26 gives no session count.

minimumRIR.rationale: No source defines a reps-in-reserve gate for progression. ACSM09 (p. 690; Table 2) adds load once the lifter can do 1-2 reps beyond the target; ACSM26 (Discussion, effort paragraph) proposes 2-3 RIR as sufficient effort. A top-of-range set with 2 or more reps in reserve satisfies both readings.

maximumIncreaseFraction.note: Top of the 2-10% range, which ACSM09 reserves for large-muscle-mass exercises. It asks for less on small-muscle-mass exercises but gives no number, and this one cap applies to every exercise, including the curl. Cited only to a narrative review.

historyDays.rationale: No source says how long a performance record stays valid for prescription (research section 7). The detraining evidence measures lost adaptation instead: IVERSEN21 (detraining section; low certainty, underlying sources unverified) says gains are preserved only briefly, under about 3 weeks. Records older than 21 days are treated as stale.

maximumGapDays.rationale: No source addresses it. At the template's minimum of 2 sessions a week (ACSM26), comparable sessions are at most 4-5 days apart; 7 days lets a streak survive one missed session but not a missed week.

supportedGoals.locator: Title and Abstract; Table 6 (strength and hypertrophy columns)

minDaysPerWeek.note: ACSM09 agrees for novices: whole body 2-3 days a week (Evidence A).

maxDaysPerWeek.locator: Strength 'Frequency', p. 693; hypertrophy 'Frequency', p. 695; Table 2, p. 700 (Evidence A)
maxDaysPerWeek.note: Novice whole-body training 2-3 days a week. ACSM09 places 4 days with intermediates, and for hypertrophy with an upper/lower split, which this one repeating session is not. ACSM26 sets no upper limit.

minSessionMinutes.rationale: Warm-up plus the three required slots at the longer (strength) estimate: 4 + 3 x 10 = 34 minutes.

warmUpMinutes.rationale: Sources favour a few exercise-specific warm-up sets over a general warm-up (IVERSEN21, 'Warm-up' section; MCCRARY15) and give no minutes. Two light sets of the first exercise, 2 x (8 reps x 4 s + 60 s) = about 3 minutes, plus 1 minute of set-up.

requiredRoles.note: At minimum one squat or leg-press pattern, one upper-body pull and one upper-body push. ACSM26 (Discussion, limitations paragraph) also lists a lower-body pull; adding it needs a fourth required slot.

minSessionMinutes.rationale: The minimum session plus one more slot at the longer estimate: 34 + 10 = 44 minutes.

workingSets.locator: Hypertrophy 'Loading and Volume', p. 694; Table 2, p. 700 (1-3 sets; Evidence A)
workingSets.note: ACSM26 (Discussion, volume paragraph) advises at least 2 sets per exercise and cannot set an optimum; KRIEGER10 finds 2-3 sets beat 1. The weekly 10+ sets per muscle in ACSM26 is not reached by one exercise per region at 2-3 days a week.

lowerReps.locator: Hypertrophy 'Loading and Volume', p. 694; Table 2, p. 700 (Evidence A)
lowerReps.note: 8-12 is a sourced convention, not an optimum: ACSM26 (Table 4, load) and LOPEZ21 find similar hypertrophy across loads when sets end near failure.

upperReps.locator: Hypertrophy 'Loading and Volume', p. 694; Table 2, p. 700 (Evidence A)

restSeconds.note: A small hypertrophy benefit above 60 s and no appreciable further benefit beyond 90 s. ACSM09: 1-2 minutes (Evidence C).

estimatedMinutes.rationale: No source gives time per exercise. 3 sets x (12 reps x 4 s tempo, the slow end of ACSM09's 1-2 s up and 1-2 s down, + 90 s rest) = about 7 minutes, plus 1 minute of set-up.

workingSets.note: Strength was enhanced by 2-3 sets. KRIEGER09: 4-6 sets were not better than 2-3.

lowerReps.locator: Summary, p. 687; strength 'Loading', p. 690; Table 2, p. 700 (Evidence A)
lowerReps.note: Novice strength: 8-12 RM at 60-70% 1RM. For intermediates ACSM26 (Table 6) favours loads of 80% 1RM or more, about 9 reps or fewer on a bench press (NUZZO24). This template does not vary by experience.

upperReps.locator: Summary, p. 687; strength 'Loading', p. 690; Table 2, p. 700 (Evidence A)

restSeconds.note: Untrained: 60-120 s is enough; trained: more than 2 minutes. ACSM09 (p. 692, Evidence B) asks 2-3 minutes or more for heavy core lifts; ACSM26 found no effect of rest on strength.

estimatedMinutes.rationale: No source gives time per exercise. 3 sets x (12 reps x 4 s tempo + 120 s rest) = about 8.4 minutes, rounded up to 9, plus 1 minute of set-up.

weeklySetsFloor.note: At or above 10 sets per muscle group per week enhanced hypertrophy. IUSCA21 p. 9 agrees.

weeklySetsCeiling.note: Six pooled studies in trained men: no added benefit above about 20 weekly sets for quadriceps and biceps (triceps did benefit). ACSM26's Discussion reads PELLAND26 as diminishing returns near 18-20; that figure could not be verified at source.

timeLimitedFloor.note: A floor for time-efficient training, not an optimum. Used only when the athlete's minutes cannot hold the full weekly floor; the week is then labelled reduced.

sessionSetsCap.rationale: Adopts the only published per-session number, about 10 sets per muscle per session (IUSCA21 p. 10, expert consensus the authors say was never measured; Low). Trials in trained men found no loss at 15-18 sets per session (docs/research/training-frequency-evidence.md section 3), so 10 is the conservative end.

consecutiveDayCap.rationale: The only verified consecutive-day protocol (GOMES19, Monday-Friday per CARNEIRO24) used about 2-3 direct sets per muscle per session; FRANCO21 about 2. A cap of 3 keeps back-to-back days inside the tested dose. Training to failure slowed recovery for up to 24-48 h (MORANNAVARRO17; Low).

setsPerExerciseMin.note: The authors advise at least two sets per exercise; the optimal number could not be determined.

setsPerExerciseMax.rationale: No source sets a maximum per exercise. 2-3 versus 4-6 sets per exercise did not differ significantly for strength (KRIEGER09) or hypertrophy (KRIEGER10), so the cap stays inside the tested 4-6 range and spreads further volume across exercises.

minutesPerSet.rationale: SCHOENFELD19V (full text, RT Procedures) gives about 1.9 min per set for 8-12-rep sets with 90 s rests: 2.0 for hypertrophy, whose prescription rests 90 s. The strength prescription rests 120 s, 30 s longer per set: 2.5. No warm-up is included; it is added separately.

warmUpMinutes.rationale: Sources favour a few exercise-specific warm-up sets over a general warm-up (IVERSEN21, 'Warm-up' section; MCCRARY15) and give no minutes. Two light sets of the first exercise, 2 x (8 reps x 4 s + 60 s) = about 3 minutes, plus 1 minute of set-up.

maxSessionsPerWeek.rationale: No qualifying trial tested conventional resistance training on 7 days a week (DANKEL17F; NUZZO24MD Table 7 covers only brief bodyweight sessions in older adults; independent search 2026-09-24). Six days a week matched three at equal volume (SARIC19; COLQUHOUN18). Seven free days are a valid input; a week uses up to six of them.

strengthExposuresMin.note: Two or more training days a week enhanced strength. Read per muscle as the owner's interpretation.

targets.rationale: Everyone aims at least at the cited weekly floor of 10 sets per muscle (ACSM26 Table 6). Intermediates aiming at hypertrophy aim a little higher because weekly volume shows a graded dose-response with diminishing returns (SCHOENFELD17V; BAZVALLE22 up to about 20). Strength gains rise less with volume beyond 2-3 sets per exercise (KRIEGER09; ACSM26 Discussion), so strength stays at the floor and relies on at least two sessions a week.

windowDays.rationale: No source sets how long to watch attendance before changing a plan. Four weeks averages out one busy week yet acts before a long gap; how quickly adaptations fade after stopping is reported inconsistently (IVERSEN21, detraining section). Only logged sessions count.

minimumPlanAgeDays.rationale: A new week is judged only after two full weeks of it, so the first adjustment reflects the plan rather than the first days of learning it.

missedSessionsPerWeek.rationale: A week fitted to attendance is proposed once the athlete completes, on average, at least one session a week fewer than planned. At equal weekly volume, fewer sessions give similar hypertrophy (ACSM26, Results 'Improving hypertrophy'), so fitting the week to real attendance keeps the weekly work instead of losing it to missed days. It is a proposal the athlete may reject; a rejected one is not repeated for the same plan.

majorMuscles.rationale: ACSM26 (Discussion, limitations paragraph) asks programmes to cover upper-body push and pull and lower-body push and pull. These six muscles are the prime movers of those regions and carry the weekly floor; arms and calves are trained as synergists and by accessories.

roles.rationale: Each role counts a set fully for its prime movers and half for synergists, following PELLAND26's best-fitting model (Abstract; Low). The hinge counts fully for hamstrings and glutes because squats and leg presses give the hamstrings little stimulus (SCHOENFELD19S, Conclusions), which is why the hinge and knee flexion carry them.

fallbacks.rationale: ACSM26 (Discussion, limitations paragraph) treats horizontal and vertical upper-body work as optional per session or per week, so an athlete without a vertical pull or press gets the horizontal one instead. A missing single-leg or knee-flexion exercise falls back to the bilateral squat or the hinge that trains the same prime movers.

sessions.rationale: Session contents follow docs/research/training-frequency-evidence.md, 'Movement roles each structure needs': ACSM26 (Discussion) for upper and lower push and pull; IVERSEN21 (Table 1) for a minimum of one lower-body exercise, one upper push and one upper pull; IUSCA21 (Table 1) for multiple planes and multi- plus single-joint work. Full body alternates horizontal (A) and vertical (B) upper-body work so both appear each week.

splits.rationale: Full body is tested at 2-3 days (ACSM09 novices; LASEVICIUS19; SCHOENFELD15) and 5 days (GOMES19). Split and full-body routines give similar gains at equal volume (RAMOSCAMPO24; PEDERSEN22), and ACSM09 lists a 4-day upper/lower split. Push/pull/legs at 6 days rests on one 10-person pilot (RIBEIRO15). The hybrids are owner combinations of these; every week they build must still pass the weekly guardrails.

splitNames.rationale: Display names only; no training effect is claimed.

ranking.rationale: Orders options only; every option already keeps the cited guardrails. Weekly volume weighs most because it is the main driver of hypertrophy (ACSM26 Table 6; SCHOENFELD17V). Exposures weigh more for strength, which rose with frequency where hypertrophy did not (ACSM26 Table 4; PELLAND26 Abstract). Recovery penalises the same muscle on back-to-back days (MORANNAVARRO17), and spread favours even spacing of each muscle's sessions, matching the at-least-48 h spacing of tested designs where free days allow (PEDERSEN22; LASEVICIUS19; IUSCA21 p. 9). Variety rewards horizontal and vertical work, hinge and single-leg coverage (ACSM26 Discussion; IUSCA21 Table 1). Adherence and stated preference are product choices, not training-effect claims: they favour a week the athlete is likely to complete.
